blogPosts.title: Building a Custom Home in Ocean Grove: Your Complete Guide for 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Everything you need to know about building a custom home in Ocean Grove VIC, from council permits and coastal design considerations to budgeting and material selection on the Bellarine Peninsula.
body: Ocean Grove has become one of the most sought-after locations on the Bellarine Peninsula for families looking to build their dream home. With its stunning coastal landscapes, relaxed community atmosphere, and proximity to both Geelong and the Great Ocean Road, it is no surprise that custom home builds in Ocean Grove are on the rise. The suburb offers a unique blend of beachside living and rural tranquillity, making it ideal for architectural homes that take full advantage of the natural surroundings. If you are considering building a custom home in Ocean Grove VIC, understanding the local landscape, council requirements, and construction considerations is essential to a successful project.

Before any construction begins in Ocean Grove, you will need to navigate the planning permit process with the Borough of Queenscliffe. The local council has specific guidelines around building in coastal areas, including setback requirements from the coastline, vegetation overlay controls, and environmental significance overlays that may affect your block. Engaging a builder who understands these local planning requirements early in the process can save you months of delays. At Duncan Pascoe Builders, we work closely with local planning consultants to ensure every application meets the borough's standards. From concept design through to permit approval, our Ocean Grove team manages the entire process so you can focus on the exciting parts of your build.

Ocean Grove's coastal position means your custom home must be designed with the local environment firmly in mind. Salt-laden winds, strong UV exposure, and the occasional storm surge all play a role in determining the right design approach for your Bellarine Peninsula property. Orienting your home to capture natural light while providing shelter from prevailing winds is a key consideration in Ocean Grove. Many of our clients choose designs that maximise views towards the coast or the Barwon River while incorporating deep eaves, quality insulation, and cross-ventilation to manage the Australian climate. A well-designed custom home in Ocean Grove should feel connected to its environment while standing up to the coastal conditions for decades.

Selecting the right building materials is critical for any Ocean Grove custom home, particularly given the coastal exposure. Marine-grade stainless steel fixings, fibre cement cladding, and treated timber are popular choices that withstand the salt air without constant maintenance. Double-glazed windows and quality insulation help regulate internal temperatures through Ocean Grove's warm summers and cool winters. At Duncan Pascoe Builders, we guide our Ocean Grove clients through every material selection decision, balancing durability, aesthetics, and budget. We source materials from trusted Bellarine Peninsula and Geelong suppliers who understand what performs best in this coastal environment. Getting the materials right from the start means your Ocean Grove home will age beautifully with minimal upkeep.

The cost of building a custom home in Ocean Grove varies significantly based on size, design complexity, site conditions, and finishes. As a rough guide, custom builds on the Bellarine Peninsula typically range from $2,000 to $3,500 per square metre, with architecturally designed homes often sitting at the higher end. Additional costs to consider in Ocean Grove include site preparation, which can vary depending on soil conditions and slope, council fees, utility connections, and landscaping. Working with a transparent builder who provides detailed upfront quoting helps you avoid surprises. Duncan Pascoe Builders provides comprehensive, itemised quotes for every Ocean Grove project so you know exactly where your investment is going before a single slab is poured.

Choosing the right builder for your Ocean Grove custom home is perhaps the most important decision you will make. A local builder who understands the Bellarine Peninsula's unique conditions, council requirements, and supplier network will deliver a smoother, more efficient build. Duncan Pascoe Builders has been constructing boutique architectural homes in Ocean Grove and surrounding suburbs for over 15 years, earning the trust of local architects, designers, and homeowners alike. Our hands-on approach means Duncan personally oversees every project, ensuring the architectural intent is honoured and the quality meets the highest standard. If you are ready to start your custom home journey in Ocean Grove, contact us for a free consultation today.

blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Renovation Cost in Ocean Grove, VIC?
blogPosts.excerpt: A detailed breakdown of home renovation costs in Ocean Grove, covering kitchen upgrades, bathroom remodels, full extensions, and structural changes on the Bellarine Peninsula.
body: Renovating a home in Ocean Grove is a popular choice for homeowners who love their location but need more space, modern amenities, or a refreshed aesthetic. Whether you are looking to extend a period cottage near the town centre or completely transform a coastal property with panoramic views, understanding the cost of a home renovation in Ocean Grove is the essential first step. Renovation costs on the Bellarine Peninsula are influenced by the scope of work, existing structural conditions, material selections, and the complexity of any design changes. On average, Ocean Grove homeowners can expect to invest between $150,000 and $500,000 for a significant renovation, though smaller kitchen and bathroom upgrades may start from $30,000.

The most common renovation projects in Ocean Grove tend to focus on opening up living spaces to capture coastal views, adding second-storey extensions for growing families, and modernising kitchens and bathrooms. Many older homes in Ocean Grove were built with smaller, compartmentalised floor plans that do not suit modern family living. Removing internal walls, installing large sliding doors, and creating open-plan kitchen-dining areas are frequent requests from our Bellarine Peninsula clients. Bathroom renovations in Ocean Grove also tend to incorporate quality, moisture-resistant materials suited to the coastal climate. Whatever the scope, a clear plan and realistic budget are the foundations of a successful renovation in Ocean Grove VIC.

Breaking down the cost of your Ocean Grove renovation, labour typically accounts for 40 to 50 percent of the total budget, with materials making up the remainder. Structural work such as removing load-bearing walls, adding steel beams, or underpinning foundations will significantly increase costs. Kitchen renovations in Ocean Grove generally range from $25,000 to $60,000 depending on cabinetry, benchtops, and appliance selections, while bathroom renovations typically fall between $20,000 and $50,000. Full home renovations on the Bellarine Peninsula, including structural changes, new roofing, updated electrical and plumbing, and quality finishes, can range from $300,000 to over $700,000. At Duncan Pascoe Builders, we provide detailed, transparent quotes for every Ocean Grove renovation project.

Ocean Grove's coastal location introduces specific considerations that affect both the scope and cost of your renovation. Existing homes near the coast may have experienced salt air corrosion on metal fixtures, timber weathering, or moisture ingress that needs addressing before cosmetic upgrades begin. Upgrading insulation, replacing windows with double-glazed units, and improving ventilation are wise investments for Ocean Grove renovations that improve comfort and energy efficiency year-round. Selecting materials that withstand the Bellarine Peninsula's coastal conditions will also save money on maintenance over time. At Duncan Pascoe Builders, we assess every Ocean Grove renovation property for these coastal factors during our initial consultation, ensuring your budget accounts for everything needed to deliver a lasting, high-quality result.

Most significant renovations in Ocean Grove will require a planning permit from the Borough of Queenscliffe, particularly if you are changing the external appearance, adding floor area, or altering the structure. Building permits are mandatory for structural work, plumbing alterations, and electrical changes in Ocean Grove. The permit process typically takes eight to twelve weeks, so factor this into your renovation timeline from the outset. Working with an experienced Ocean Grove builder who understands local council requirements will streamline the approval process considerably. Duncan Pascoe Builders manages all permit applications for our Bellarine Peninsula renovation projects, ensuring compliance with local building regulations and Australian standards so your renovation proceeds smoothly from design to completion.

A successful home renovation in Ocean Grove starts with choosing a builder who understands the unique character of Bellarine Peninsula homes and the coastal environment they exist in. Duncan Pascoe Builders has completed numerous renovations across Ocean Grove, Barwon Heads, and Queenscliff, ranging from subtle modernisation to full-scale transformations. Our project management approach means every trade, every material delivery, and every council inspection is coordinated efficiently, keeping your renovation on time and on budget. We take pride in our communication, providing regular updates and transparent reporting throughout the process. If you are planning a home renovation in Ocean Grove, contact Duncan Pascoe Builders for a free on-site consultation and detailed quote.

blogPosts.title: Ocean Grove Building Permits: Everything You Need to Know Before You Build
blogPosts.excerpt: A comprehensive guide to planning and building permits in Ocean Grove, covering the Borough of Queenscliffe process, coastal overlays, and how to get your project approved efficiently.
body: If you are planning to build, renovate, or extend a property in Ocean Grove, understanding the permit process is a critical first step. The Borough of Queenscliffe governs all planning and building permits in Ocean Grove, and the region has specific regulations that reflect its unique coastal and heritage character. Whether you are constructing a brand-new custom home, adding an extension, or making structural changes to an existing property, you will almost certainly need one or both types of permits. Navigating the Ocean Grove permit process without expert guidance can lead to costly delays, compliance issues, and frustration. Partnering with a local builder who knows the borough's requirements inside and out will save you time and money.

In Victoria, planning permits and building permits serve different purposes, and most Ocean Grove projects require both. A planning permit from the Borough of Queenscliffe assesses whether your proposed work is acceptable in terms of its impact on the neighbourhood, streetscape, and environment. This includes considerations like setbacks, building height, site coverage, and visual bulk. A building permit, issued by a registered building surveyor, ensures your construction meets the Building Code of Australia and relevant Australian standards. In Ocean Grove, planning permits are typically required for new dwellings, significant extensions, changes to external appearance, and any work within overlay zones. Understanding which permits apply to your Ocean Grove project early prevents unexpected roadblocks.

Ocean Grove properties are subject to several overlay zones that can affect what you are permitted to build and where. The coastal interface overlay, environmental significance overlay, and vegetation protection overlay are commonly applied across Ocean Grove and the wider Bellarine Peninsula. These overlays may restrict building height, require additional setbacks from the coastline, mandate native vegetation retention, or require detailed environmental assessments. Heritage overlays also apply to certain areas of the Borough of Queenscliffe, affecting what modifications can be made to existing structures. Before commencing any project in Ocean Grove, a thorough review of your property's zoning and overlay controls is essential. Duncan Pascoe Builders assists Ocean Grove clients with this assessment as part of our comprehensive pre-build planning service.

Ocean Grove's position on the Bellarine Peninsula means that coastal management and environmental considerations play a significant role in the permit process. The Borough of Queenscliffe works closely with coastal management authorities to ensure new development does not adversely affect the fragile coastal ecosystem. Properties near the Ocean Grove coastline may face additional requirements regarding stormwater management, dune protection, and setback distances from the high water mark. Bushfire attack level assessments may also be required for properties bordered by native vegetation. These environmental factors add complexity to the Ocean Grove permit process that inexperienced builders often underestimate. At Duncan Pascoe Builders, we have extensive experience navigating these coastal requirements, ensuring your Ocean Grove project meets every regulatory obligation.

The permit application process in Ocean Grove typically follows a structured timeline. Once your plans are prepared by a registered architect or building designer, your planning permit application is submitted to the Borough of Queenscliffe. The council assesses the application, which may include a public notification period where neighbours can provide feedback. This phase generally takes eight to twelve weeks for a standard application in Ocean Grove. Following planning approval, your building permit application is lodged with a registered building surveyor, adding another two to four weeks. Total permit time for an Ocean Grove project typically ranges from ten to sixteen weeks. Early engagement with your builder helps streamline this process and keeps your project moving forward.

The most effective way to navigate Ocean Grove's building permit process is to work with an experienced local builder from the very beginning of your project. Duncan Pascoe Builders has built strong relationships with the Borough of Queenscliffe planning department, local building surveyors, and environmental consultants across the Bellarine Peninsula. We manage the complete permit process for our Ocean Grove clients, from initial site assessments and zoning reviews through to application preparation and liaison with council. Our deep understanding of Ocean Grove's specific overlay controls and coastal building requirements means fewer surprises and faster approvals. Contact Duncan Pascoe Builders today to discuss your Ocean Grove building project and let us handle the permit process from start to finish.

blogPosts.title: Best Building Materials for Ocean Grove's Coastal Climate: A Local Builder's Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Expert advice on selecting the right building materials for Ocean Grove's coastal environment, covering cladding, roofing, windows, framing, and interior finishes that withstand the Bellarine Peninsula conditions.
body: Choosing the right building materials for your Ocean Grove home is about far more than aesthetics. The Bellarine Peninsula's coastal climate presents unique challenges that directly impact the longevity, maintenance requirements, and overall performance of the materials you select. Salt-laden winds, high UV exposure, variable humidity, and occasional severe weather events all take their toll on building materials in Ocean Grove. Homes closer to the coastline face even more demanding conditions, making material selection a critical decision that affects both upfront cost and long-term durability. As a builder with over 15 years of experience constructing homes in Ocean Grove, Duncan Pascoe Builders has seen firsthand which materials stand up to the coastal environment and which fall short.

For exterior cladding in Ocean Grove, the most durable options include fibre cement sheeting, weatherboard with quality paint systems, and masonry. Fibre cement products such as James Hardie cladding are popular choices for Ocean Grove homes because they resist moisture, salt air, and termites without warping or deteriorating. Rendered masonry provides excellent durability and thermal mass benefits, making it well-suited to the Bellarine Peninsula's temperature variations. Traditional timber weatherboard remains a beloved choice for Ocean Grove's coastal aesthetic, but it requires a high-quality paint or stain system and regular maintenance to withstand the salt exposure. At Duncan Pascoe Builders, we help Ocean Grove homeowners select cladding that balances coastal durability with the visual character they want for their home.

Roofing material selection in Ocean Grove needs to account for salt corrosion, wind resistance, and thermal performance. Colorbond steel roofing in a coastal-rated finish is one of the most popular choices for Bellarine Peninsula homes, offering excellent corrosion resistance and a wide range of colours suited to the Ocean Grove landscape. Concrete and terracotta roof tiles also perform well in coastal conditions, though the weight implications must be considered in the structural design. For Ocean Grove homes, we recommend selecting roofing materials rated for coastal environments and ensuring all fixings are marine-grade stainless steel or galvanised to prevent rust. Proper roof insulation paired with the right roofing material will keep your Ocean Grove home comfortable through every season.

Windows are one of the most important material decisions for any Ocean Grove home, given the coastal exposure and the desire to maximise natural light and views. Double-glazed aluminium windows with a powder-coated coastal finish are an excellent choice for Ocean Grove properties, providing thermal efficiency, noise reduction, and resistance to salt corrosion. Timber-framed windows offer a warm, natural aesthetic but require ongoing maintenance in the coastal environment. For Ocean Grove homes facing the ocean or Barwon River, consider awning or hopper-style windows that can be opened for ventilation while managing wind-driven rain. At Duncan Pascoe Builders, we specify windows for every Ocean Grove project based on orientation, exposure, and the client's lifestyle requirements.

The structural timber and framing materials used in your Ocean Grove home must be treated to resist the coastal conditions. H3 treated pine framing is the standard for external applications in Ocean Grove, providing termite and rot resistance suited to the Bellarine Peninsula's climate. For homes in closer proximity to the coast, upgrading to H4 treatment for ground-contact applications adds an extra layer of protection. Steel framing is an alternative that eliminates concerns about moisture and termites entirely, though it requires careful management of thermal bridging. Engineered timber products such as LVL beams and particleboard flooring perform well in Ocean Grove when properly sealed and protected. Selecting the right structural materials ensures your home's frame stands strong for decades.

Interior material selection in Ocean Grove should balance coastal durability with comfort and style. Porcelain and natural stone tiles are excellent choices for bathrooms, laundries, and entryways in Ocean Grove homes, handling moisture and sand tracked in from the beach without showing wear. Quality vinyl plank flooring offers a waterproof, low-maintenance alternative that mimics the look of timber without the susceptibility to coastal humidity fluctuations. For kitchen benchtops, engineered stone and porcelain slabs provide the durability needed in an active Ocean Grove household while maintaining a premium appearance. Paint selections for interior walls should include low-VOC options with mould-resistant formulations, particularly important in Ocean Grove's humid summer months.

Sourcing building materials locally in Ocean Grove and the wider Bellarine Peninsula offers significant advantages for your construction project. Local suppliers understand the specific demands of the coastal environment and can recommend products proven to perform in Ocean Grove conditions. Working with Geelong and Bellarine-based suppliers also reduces delivery times and costs, keeping your project on schedule. At Duncan Pascoe Builders, we have established strong relationships with trusted material suppliers across the Bellarine Peninsula, ensuring our Ocean Grove clients receive quality products at competitive prices. We guide every client through the material selection process, providing samples and expert advice to help you make informed decisions that will keep your Ocean Grove home looking and performing beautifully for years to come.
